sections.title: Infrastructure as the Key to Economic Leapfrogging
sections.body: Africa's tech story is often framed around apps, but the real value is shifting to the physical infrastructure layer. Our deep-dive analysis reveals that the East African Community (EAC) is currently at a critical 'Digital Inflection Point.' As fiber-to-the-home and 5G penetration explode, the backend compute capacity has not kept pace. This creates a massive opportunity for projects like Kenya AI Compute to act as the regional 'Compute Utility.' We explore how the rise of localized AI—for Swahili language models, regional agricultural analytics, and African-centric fintech—is driving a localized GPU demand that cannot be served by servers in Dublin or Marseille. By building the infrastructure here, we are not just saving costs; we are enabling a new category of African tech giants that could never exist in a high-latency environment. items: Demographics: 1.4B people, the world's youngest and most tech-native population.
